title: Database Indexing
subtitle: One index turns a 3-second scan into 3 milliseconds, and every extra index taxes each write
motto: Index what you look up, and only what you look up
keyInsight: An index trades write cost and space for read speed, and it only helps queries that pick out a small share of the table.

decisions.title: Show an index that loses
decisions.description: The failure frame runs the index on a query returning 30% of rows, where random fetches make it slower than a scan.
decisions.alternatives: Showing only the equality lookup would suggest an index never hurts a read.

decisions.title: Count writes, not just reads
decisions.description: The last frame reports write amplification, because each index is one more write per row change.
decisions.alternatives: Reporting read latency alone would hide the cost that grows with every index added.
